body:
Google added a new way to control which campaign gets your budget first, in "Guide your campaign spending with new priority and allocation features."

Most people will read that as a feature update. It is actually a question about where your money goes when it is tight.

Here is the part worth your Monday: budget priority is not the same as a Performance goal. One tells Google which campaign gets funded first when you don't have enough for all of them. The other tells Google what a "win" looks like inside each campaign. Most accounts have only ever set the second one.

If you run more than one campaign and you have never touched priority, Google has been deciding the order for you. That is not a judgement on Google. It is just a setting nobody opens because nothing forces you to.

Cost per lead means nothing if the campaign funding your best leads is the one getting starved first. Check which campaign is marked top priority before you check anything else this week.

slides.text: Google just let you rank your own campaigns by priority.
Most people will read this as a small feature update. It is not.
Every account with more than one campaign splits a budget between them, whether you choose how or not.
Before this, that split followed Google's own rules, mostly invisible to you.
Now there is a setting that says: fund this campaign first, before any other.
That is different from a Performance goal, the setting that tells Google what counts as a win.
Priority decides who gets paid first. Goal decides what paying off looks like.
Most accounts have set the second one and never touched the first.
If your best campaign has been starved while a weak one got funded, this is why.
Open Google Ads, go to each campaign's settings, and look for the new priority and allocation controls before you touch anything else.
